extraction.name: SciQ
extraction.description: A dataset of 13,679 multiple choice science exam questions crowdsourced from science study textbooks and existing science questions, with associated passages for direct-answer use.
extraction.license: Creative Commons Attribution-Non-Commercial 3.0 Unported (CC BY-NC 3.0) for CK-12 books; dataset release license not explicitly stated in the paper
extraction.creator: Johannes Welbl, Nelson F. Liu, Matt Gardner
extraction.citeAs: Welbl, J., Liu, N. F., & Gardner, M. Crowdsourcing Multiple Choice Science Questions.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created in a two-step crowdsourcing process: first, crowd workers selected one of three filtered textbook paragraphs and wrote a question answerable from it; second, another worker reviewed the question-answer pair and selected up to two model-suggested distractors and wrote at least one additional distractor to form a multiple-choice question.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: A small percentage of passages were obtained from unreleasable texts, so the direct-answer version is slightly smaller than the multiple-choice version.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Science study textbooks and other online learning resources (including CK-12 and OpenStax) were used as the base corpus; existing science exam questions were also used to train the distractor model.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: A rule-based document filter was applied to paragraphs before crowdsourcing; the filter removed sentences with questions/exclamations, missing verb phrases, modal verbs, imperative phrases, demonstratives, non-third-person pronouns, first names, extreme length, special characters, graphs/tables/web links, discourse markers, absolute wording, and instructional vocabulary.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Filtered textbook paragraphs were presented to workers; workers could choose one of three paragraphs or reject all if irrelevant. For the distractor task, workers were shown the question-answer pair and six model-suggested distractors, could select up to two, and had to write at least one distractor themselves.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowd workers authored questions from passages and created distractors for multiple-choice answers. Workers also validated whether generated questions were suitable for a school science exam.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper reports that 92.8% of generated question-answer pairs passed validation, workers accepted model-suggested distractors about half the time, and 36.1% of final distractors were generated by the model. A qualitative evaluation found humans identified the real exam question only 55% of the time.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Each multiple-choice item has one question, one correct answer, and three distractors; in the distractor task, workers could select up to two of six suggested distractors and had to write at least one of their own.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Crowd workers on Amazon Mechanical Turk with Master's status; 175 workers participated in the project.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: A noisy classifier for passage selection and a random forest distractor ranking model implemented with scikit-learn; features included GloVe embeddings, WordNet-based indicators, OpenIE/KB features, and lexical similarity features.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to improve science question answering and support research on medium-data settings and transfer to real science exams.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that crowd workers may lack domain expertise and that poorly chosen distractors can make questions trivial; it also discusses the need to avoid irrelevant or overly specific textbook passages.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Some passages came from unreleasable texts, making the direct-answer version smaller. The dataset is focused on science exam questions and may not generalize beyond that domain. Neural models did not outperform a simple IR baseline on the multiple-choice version.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, and testing for multiple-choice science QA and direct-answer reading comprehension; also used as additional training data to improve performance on real 4th- and 8th-grade science exam questions.
